name: Jacob Leibholz
record: *** BIRTH ENTRY FOUND AND READ AT THE IMAGE, 22 September 2026. *** Standesamt Schubin, Geburtsregister 1884, AKT NR. 63, page marked A.64. Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy, Urząd Stanu Cywilnego Szubin Miasto, sygnatura 28, "Akta urodzeń - pierwopis nr 1-97", scan 64 of the unit on genealogiawarchiwach.pl. Registered at Schubin on 11 AUGUST 1884; the child was born on 8 AUGUST 1884, of male sex, and given the forename JACOB.

name: Sally Leibholz
record: NAMED IN HIS SON'S BIRTH ENTRY AS THE INFORMANT, and he registered the birth himself. The register calls him "DER KAUFMANN SALLY LEIBHOLZ", resident at Schubin, MOSAISCHER RELIGION, and HE SIGNED THE ENTRY IN HIS OWN HAND — the signature "Sally Leibholz" is on the page above the registrar's. *** THIS DATES HIS TRADE. *** The archive knew him as a merchant only from later and looser sources; here a registrar writes KAUFMANN against his name in August 1884.

name: Friederike Leibholz née Schmul
record: NAMED IN THE SAME ENTRY AS THE MOTHER, in the register's own words "FRIEDERIKE LEIBHOLZ GEBORENE SCHMUL", seiner Ehefrau, MOSAISCHER RELIGION, "wohnhaft bei ihm dem Anzeigenden" — living with the informant at Schubin. The maiden name SCHMUL is written plainly and is not an inference.

name: *** WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW HERE, AND IT IS NOT THE PARENTS ***
record: THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD ALL THREE PEOPLE AND THE LINK BETWEEN THEM, from the family record: Jacob born 8 August 1884, son of Sally Leibholz born 7 July 1847 and Friederike Schmul. NONE OF THAT IS A DISCOVERY. What changes is its STANDING: until today the parentage of Jacob Leibholz rested on a family tree, and it now rests on the civil register of the town he was born in, read at the image. A tree is a claim; this is a document, and the two agree to the day.

name: and five things the tree did not have
record: (1) SALLY'S TRADE IN 1884 — Kaufmann. (2) BOTH PARENTS' RELIGION AS THE STATE RECORDED IT — mosaisch, written by the registrar against each of them. (3) THE REGISTRATION DATE, 11 August, three days after the birth. (4) THE FAMILY'S RESIDENCE — both parents living together at Schubin in August 1884. (5) SALLY'S OWN SIGNATURE, which is the first specimen of his hand this archive has.

name: and it corroborates the marriage independently
record: The portal's single indexed Leibholz is a MARRIAGE at Szubin — unit 6/1792/0/2.2/141, page 10. This birth entry, written ten years later, calls the mother "geborene Schmul" and the father's wife, which is exactly what a Sally Leibholz × Friederike Schmul marriage at Szubin on 24 November 1874 would produce. TWO RECORDS, TEN YEARS APART, AGREEING WITHOUT EITHER BEING DERIVED FROM THE OTHER.

name: *** WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THE LETTER WAS SENT TO ANSWER ***
record: A GERMAN BIRTH ENTRY NAMES THE PARENTS AND NOT THEIR ORIGINS. There is no birthplace, no age and no former residence for either Sally or Friederike on this page. So the standing question — WHETHER THE SCHUBIN LEIBHOLZ ARE A HAMMERSTEIN FAMILY THAT MOVED EAST — IS NOT ANSWERED BY THIS DOCUMENT and still rests where it rested: on the Gedenkbuch, and on Sally's recorded birth at Hammerstein in 1847 which no surviving register can now confirm, Koszalin having stated on 16 September that the Hammerstein books do not exist.

name: where the answer would have to come from now
record: THE 1874 MARRIAGE ENTRY, which is the next thing to read and is on the same portal. A German marriage entry gives each party's AGE, BIRTHPLACE and PARENTS. If Sally Leibholz married at Szubin in 1874, that page says where he was born and who his father was — and it would settle Hammerstein in a line.

name: source
